channel.title: The Ashgrove Times — The News Desk
channel.description: For the Fellers — the morning paper, filed daily at 7:00 AM ET.

item.title: No. 32 — Trump sends Witkoff and Kushner to Moscow with a plan to end the war
item.description: Zelenskyy halts strikes on Russia during the envoys' visit and asks Moscow to do the same before their Sunday stop in Kyiv.

item.title: No. 31 — Vance rules out Iran talks until attacks on shipping stop
item.description: Kuwait says it intercepted Iranian missiles and drones; Brent holds near $96 as Hormuz transits lag pre-war.

item.title: No. 30 — Iran hits U.S. bases in Kuwait and UAE as Trump vows more strikes
item.description: Iran puts its toll from this week's U.S. strikes at 18 dead; Tehran says it laid new mines south of Hormuz.

item.title: No. 29 — U.S. widens strikes on Iran; Tehran answers at bases in three countries
item.description: Iran says one strike hit a wedding near the Strait of Hormuz, killing at least 5; Jordan intercepted 10 missiles.

item.title: No. 28 — Jury convicts Duane Davis of first-degree murder in Tupac Shakur's killing
item.description: Deliberations took less than three hours; Davis, 63, is the only person ever charged in the 30-year-old case.

item.title: No. 27 — U.S. and Iran trade fire over the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: CENTCOM hit launchers it says were set to mine the strait; Jordan intercepted eight missiles fired back at bases hosting U.S. forces.

item.title: No. 26 — Nepal warns of new flooding as border disaster toll passes 750
item.description: Disaster authority cites rising water upstream; 734 dead and 2,498 missing in Nepal alone

item.title: No. 25 — Rescue resumes on Nepal-Tibet border as flood toll passes 630
item.description: Nearly 3,000 people are missing after crews paused for a day while an unstable barrier lake overflowed

item.title: No. 24 — Nepal flood toll passes 470 as a barrier lake threatens new deluge
item.description: More than 1,500 are missing across Nepal and Tibet, and a blocked river is swelling above the disaster zone

item.title: No. 23 — Glacial flood kills at least 160 in Nepal, hundreds missing
item.description: An ice avalanche dammed and released a Himalayan river; the Trishuli rose 27 feet in half an hour

item.title: No. 22 — Dolly Parton, country music's great ambassador, dies at 80
item.description: The singer, songwriter and philanthropist died in Nashville after a brief battle with cancer, her representatives said

item.title: No. 21 — Treasury launches 'Operation Economic Outcast' against Iran
item.description: Nearly 60 entities and vessels sanctioned; Trump to press foreign leaders to cut Tehran off

item.title: No. 20 — Wildfire on Reno's edge forces tens of thousands to evacuate
item.description: The human-caused Hawk Fire burned 15,000 acres with no containment; the National Guard is mobilized

item.title: No. 19 — Canada sets dollar-for-dollar tariffs on U.S. goods for Sept. 8
item.description: Carney says Washington 'asked too much and offered too little' after 50% U.S. duties took effect

item.title: No. 18 — U.S. imposes 50% tariffs on Canada as talks collapse at deadline
item.description: Carney suspended negotiations and said Canada will match the duties dollar for dollar.

item.title: No. 17 — Treasury yields hit their highest since 2007 as stocks fall
item.description: The same bond paid 1.7% in 2021. Thirty-year mortgages are now past 6.6%.

item.title: No. 16 — Russian missile barrage kills at least 12 in Kyiv
item.description: A nine-story block collapsed in Solomianskyi district and a children's hospital was damaged.

item.title: No. 15 — Donalds and Jolly win Florida primaries for governor
item.description: Moody and Nixon take the Senate nominations as DeSantis reaches his term limit

item.title: No. 14 — U.S.-Iran truce memorandum expires with no talks under way
item.description: Neither side proposed an extension, and the Strait of Hormuz stays closed.

item.title: No. 13 — Kushner meets Hamas chief in Cairo before Netanyahu talks
item.description: Hamas would disarm and Israeli forces withdraw. Netanyahu rejected the plan last week.

item.title: No. 12 — Flores quake toll climbs to 51 as thousands leave home
item.description: Indonesia counts 341 aftershocks two days after a magnitude 7.7 struck off the island

item.title: No. 11 — Magnitude 7.7 quake off Flores kills at least 20 in Indonesia
item.description: Landslides cut the island's main highway; a tsunami warning was lifted after no sea-level change.

item.title: No. 10 — Iran rejects Trump's Hormuz claim as two more tankers are hit
item.description: The UAE called the attacks piracy; 15 of the company's ships have been hit since February.

item.title: No. 9 — Millions watch Spain's first total solar eclipse since 1912
item.description: Totality ran about a minute over Spain under cloudless skies; much of Iceland was clouded over.

item.title: No. 8 — Democrats pick a progressive in Minnesota, a centrist in Wisconsin
item.description: Flanagan will face Republican Michele Tafoya, a former sports broadcaster, in November.

item.title: No. 7 — Magnitude 7.4 quake kills 132 across western Colombia
item.description: President Abelardo de la Espriella, sworn in three days earlier, declared a state of emergency; Cali imposed a curfew.

item.title: No. 6 — Shanghai takes its heaviest rain in 150 years as Dolphin moves inland
item.description: More than a million people were moved out ahead of the storm, which came ashore in Zhejiang late Sunday.

item.title: No. 5 — Iran sets six conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Tehran's terms reach past the June memorandum even as an Oman corridor deal nears

item.title: No. 4 — Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan sign mutual defense pact in Mecca
item.description: The Makkah agreement treats an attack on one as an attack on all.

item.title: No. 3 — Trump signs orders narrowing birthright citizenship
item.description: Two immigration actions follow the Supreme Court's 6-3 rejection of his first attempt in June.
